newsitem.title: USA: GM labor deal to hurt efficiency - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GM labor deal to hurt efficiency - WSJ.

text.p: The tentative three-year labor contract that General Motors Corp signed with the United Automobile Workers union will only allow the company to raise its manufacturing efficiency in 1999 to about half way where its best rivals are today, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
The newspaper quoted company officials as saying General Motors would only be able to raise efficiency to the level of their competitors by 2002.
The contract brought to an end a series of strikes designed to force the company not sell units that made car parts in its effort to improve efficiency.
The newspaper said the company could nevertheless remain competitive by cutting costs in other areas like product development and material outlays.
